scene.bubble: It's presentation day! Learn the linking words that make an argument clear, then share your voice.
scene.intro: This is the last unit of the year and presentation day for the Inspiring Nordic Trades project. In this unit you read Mateo's account of the big day, you learn the linking words that connect ideas — although, however, therefore, for example — and you prepare your own short presentation. A good project is not only about knowing things; it is about sharing them clearly. What is your voice going to say?

data.title: Our project, our voice
data.author: mateo
data.text:
Today was presentation day for our Inspiring Nordic Trades project, and it was the proudest moment of the year. Each group had ten minutes to explain what they had learned about real skills and the world of work.

Our group argued that trades and technology need each other. On the one hand, machines can produce things quickly. On the other hand, only people can design with imagination and care. Although robots are powerful, they are not creative. Therefore, we said, the future belongs to people who can do both.

Presenting was not easy. At first I was nervous; however, once I started, I forgot my fear. It really helps to organise your ideas: first, give your opinion; then, give a reason; finally, give an example. For instance, we explained how a handmade guitar can last fifty years, while a cheap one breaks in months.

Nadia showed our posters, Sofía read a short poem, and Liam answered the audience's questions with confidence. In conclusion, we learned that a good project is not only about knowing things — it is about sharing them clearly.

What is your voice going to say?

data.title: Linking words for opinions
data.intro: Good speakers and writers connect their ideas with linking words. They make an argument clear and easy to follow.

examples.text: Although robots are powerful, they aren't creative.
Machines are fast. Therefore, we use them.

rules: Although and however show a contrast (like 'but'). Although joins two clauses; however often starts a new sentence.
Therefore and so show a result (what happens next).
For example / for instance and in addition introduce examples and extra ideas.

items.sentence: ___ it was difficult, we enjoyed the project.
The talk was short. ___, it was very clear.
Machines can't be creative; ___, we need people.
We need real skills, ___ carpentry and cooking.
I was nervous. ___, I did my best.

activities.title: Open cloze — complete the advice. Write ONE word in each gap.

data.text: {1} presenting is hard, it is worth it. I was nervous; {2}, I did my best. Plan your time {3} organise your ideas. Explain your opinion, {4} it helps the audience. For {5}, say why skills matter. Robots can't create; {6}, we still need people.

data.script: Good morning, Grade 8. Today is our Inspiring Nordic presentation day. Here is how it works. Each group has ten minutes to present. Speak clearly and look at your audience. Remember to give an opinion, a reason and an example. Use linking words like 'although' and 'however' to connect your ideas. After each talk, the audience will ask two questions. Good luck — we are all very proud of you!

activities.title: Speaking — give a mini-presentation. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: Give a two-minute mini-presentation about your Inspiring Nordic year, like a B1 Speaking long turn. Model: “In my opinion, the best part was the workshop, because we learned real skills. For example, I built a wooden box.” Say: your opinion of the project, one reason and one example. Use linking words (although, however, for example, therefore). Look at your audience and speak with confidence. Then record it.

homework.prompt: Write a short opinion text (8–10 sentences) about your Inspiring Nordic year for presentation day. Give your opinion, two reasons and an example. Connect your ideas with although, however, therefore and for example. Capital letters and full stops!
